Supplies matching generalized 1:20,000,0: Supplies matching generalised 1:20,000,000 state, county and county-equivalent boundaries for the United States at zoom 7 through TIGERweb. It also supplies generalised US primary roads at zooms 6 through 16, secondary roads at zooms 8 through 16 and railway geometry at zooms 10 through 16. Levels 14 through 16 use finer source geometry. Levels 15 and 16 add Main Street segments. Level 16 also adds a bounded subset of county, other-numbered and long named local roads while excluding millions of shorter local streets. Level 17 adds a separately bounded tier of longer municipal roads as sparse overlays over complete level 16 tiles. These boundaries and transport features are simplified for geographic awareness rather than navigation, legal or high-precision use. The generated tile manifest records the source, vintage and attribution.
Supplies the simplified world overview;: Supplies the simplified world overview; global country, first-level administrative boundary, populated-place, lake, and river-centreline data; and North American roads outside the United States used to generate local SVG tiles. The water layers switch from 1:50m overview data to ranked 1:10m detail at zoom 6. At zoom 8, regional supplements add finer drainage detail across North America, Europe and Australia. The road layer adds coverage for Canada, Mexico, Central America, and parts of the Caribbean at zooms 6 through 8; U.S. roads come exclusively from the Census Bureau. Coastlines, borders, water, and roads are deliberately generalised: these maps provide enough context to recognise an area while keeping downloads small. They must not be used for surveying, navigation, or authoritative boundary decisions.

The Geo preview directly implements Web: The Geo preview directly implements Web Mercator projection, visible-tile selection, fallback scaling, longitude wrapping, panning, zooming, click-to-coordinate conversion and marker placement. It starts with a reusable SVG world overview and reads locally generated MVT 2.1 vector tiles from a range-addressable PMTiles v3 archive. The browser uses a first-party PMTiles reader, MVT decoder and Canvas renderer; no third-party mapping library is bundled. Tippecanoe is a build-time tool only. OpenStreetMap raster tiles are requested only after the user selects that view and grants consent.

When a user needs more precise visual co: When a user needs more precise visual context, the OpenStreetMap tab loads standard raster tiles for the visible area after explicit consent. This view normally shows much more local detail than the bundled vector tiles, but it sends the user's IP address, request headers, referrer and requested tile coordinates to OpenStreetMap. Its database is licensed under ODbL, and hosted tiles follow separate usage requirements.
